name_reason: Follows fd2_<domain>_<descriptor> convention (domain=render/gfx, descriptor=filled_circle_band_anim). Accurately describes the function: renders one frame of a filled circular band animation (top arc + bottom arc + solid middle band) with party characters composited on top. No Ghidra address residue in the name.
purpose: Render one frame of a filled circular band animation (top arc, bottom arc, and a solid middle row-band) with the live party characters composited on top -- the AoE-with-chars overlay look.
logic_summary: Calls fd2_render_circle_anim_row twice (top arc rows from cx; bottom arc rows from param_2) with fd2_composite_all_chars_overlay() between them to paint the party chars. Then computes the solid middle band half-width = trunc((double)param_3 * 1.6) (x87 FMUL m64[0x50208]=1.6, __CHP forces RC=round-toward-zero so FRNDINT truncates, NOT round-to-nearest -- Ghidra ROUND() macro is misleading). Clamps left edge to 0 and right edge to 0x138, then fills rows cx..param_2-1 by calling fd2_apply_palette_remap_run(radius, half_width+right_off, row_ptr) where row_ptr = large_game_state_buffer + 0x8088 + cx*0x1C8 + left_clip, advancing row_ptr by 0x1C8 (456 = workspace pitch) each iteration.
signature: void __cdecl fd2_render_filled_circle_band_anim(uint32 param_1, uint32 param_2, uint32 param_3, int cx, int cy, int radius)

params.name: param_1
params.semantics: Column center cx in workspace pixels (forwarded as 1st arg to both row calls; used as the horizontal center for the left/right clamp of the solid band).
params.reason: Generic Ghidra auto-name param_1; actual role is the column center (cx). 'col_center' reflects the horizontal-center role and carries no address residue.

params.name: param_2
params.semantics: Bottom row index = band-fill exclusive end (loop runs cx..param_2-1) and also the bottom arc's row start (passed as 5th arg to the 2nd row call).
params.reason: Generic Ghidra auto-name param_2; actual role is the bottom row index / band-fill end. 'bottom_row' is descriptive and address-free.

params.name: param_3
params.semantics: Radius factor for the band half-width: half_width = trunc((double)param_3 * 1.6). Also forwarded as 3rd arg to both row calls.
params.reason: Generic Ghidra auto-name param_3; actual role is the radius factor scaled by 1.6 to derive the band half-width. 'radius_factor' is descriptive and address-free.

params.name: cx
params.semantics: Top band-fill start row (also the top arc's row start, passed as 5th arg to the 1st row call) and the loop induction variable for the solid-band fill (cx..param_2-1).
params.reason: Ghidra label 'cx' is misleading -- it suggests a column-X but the value is a top ROW index/start; it is also the row-fill loop counter. 'top_row' matches actual semantics; current name is misleading per naming rules.

params.name: cy
params.semantics: Arc row-loop exclusive end -- forwarded as 6th arg to both fd2_render_circle_anim_row calls (the arc loop's row bound). Not used in this function's own body otherwise.
params.reason: Ghidra label 'cy' is misleading -- it suggests a center-Y but the value is the arc row-loop exclusive end passed through to the row calls. 'row_loop_end' matches actual semantics.

params.name: radius
params.semantics: Palette-remap SOURCE pointer (a uint8* color-remap table), forwarded straight through to every fd2_apply_palette_remap_run and to both fd2_render_circle_anim_row calls. Not a length despite the Ghidra label.
params.reason: Ghidra label 'radius' is strongly misleading -- the value is a palette-remap source POINTER, not a radius/length. Caller passes the handle returned by fd2_animate_warp_out_collapse and it is cast to (uint8 *) at every use. The sibling fn in the same source file already uses 'palette_remap_src' for this role; matching it keeps naming consistent and address-free.

returns.semantics: No return value. The original binary has no explicit RET in this body: on loop exit (JGE 0x21DAD) it tail-jumps into a shared POP EBP/EDI/ESI/EBX + RET sequence in the epilogue of the orphan fn @ 0x21BD0 (same PUSH EBX/ESI/EDI/EBP frame shape; Watcom merges the register-restore epilogue). The C equivalent is simply the loop running to completion.
